bug_semantics: An authenticated application user with TABLE/READ permission and a datasource ID can call GET /api/datasources/:datasourceId. The controller returns the datasource configuration after a schema-type-driven redaction pass, but MongoDB connectionString and Firebase privateKey were declared STRING while holding live credentials. Because removeSecrets masked only PASSWORD and SENSITIVE_LONGFORM fields, those STRING values survived and were returned in plaintext.
flaw_origin: Commit 28329d7f6b1f7b532665685af78e51827ac80c7e made the low-privilege single-datasource read path functional by changing the route parameter from :id to :datasourceId, matching the raw-return controller's ctx.params.datasourceId lookup. Its parent had the controller and TABLE/READ route skeleton, but the parameter mismatch prevented that lookup. At the BIC, MongoDB already stored connectionString as FIELD_TYPES.STRING; Firebase later extended the same flaw in c2d48bebd7100d7949de4555759de543a00b9256 by defining privateKey as STRING. The 2023 redaction addition b659060beb4246ad943b4660fb06f7a823d12a3d was only a partial mitigation and did not originate the reachable TABLE/READ exposure.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object identifies author and committer as mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>, has subject 'Fixing issue with datasource find endpoint, removing un-used code and updating data source test.', contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other trailers, and has no bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-6mpp-gfg5-x2vv states affected <3.40.0/patched 3.40.0 and identifies packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/datasources/datasources.ts removeSecrets, packages/server/src/integrations/mongodb.ts connectionString, packages/server/src/integrations/firebase.ts privateKey, and the TABLE/READ single-datasource route.

git show 28329d7f6b1f7b532665685af78e51827ac80c7e -- packages/server/src/api/routes/datasource.js packages/server/src/api/controllers/datasource.js shows the causal one-line route repair /api/datasources/:id -> /api/datasources/:datasourceId under authorized(PermissionTypes.TABLE, PermissionLevels.READ), while find reads ctx.params.datasourceId and returns the entire database document; the same commit adds a successful find-route test.

Direct parent-tree verification with git show dd16c84ecd6feb13b5c3489abf5eea1a218d9456:packages/server/src/api/routes/datasource.js and :packages/server/src/api/controllers/datasource.js shows route parameter :id but controller lookup ctx.params.datasourceId. Thus the BIC's matching parameter, and therefore the advisory's functional TABLE/READ read-by-ID path, is absent at the immediate parent.

git show 28329d7f6b1f7b532665685af78e51827ac80c7e:packages/server/src/integrations/mongodb.js shows connectionString declared FIELD_TYPES.STRING and passed to MongoClient. git show c2d48bebd7100d7949de4555759de543a00b9256 shows Firebase introduced privateKey as DatasourceFieldTypes.STRING and passed it into Firestore credentials.

git show b659060beb4246ad943b4660fb06f7a823d12a3d shows the first removeSecrets implementation replacing only DatasourceFieldType.PASSWORD values and wiring it into fetch/find/save/update. This reduced raw exposure but skipped the pre-existing STRING credential fields, so it is a partial mitigation rather than the BIC.

git show 330c1c9c2984bab330456b6be6921f8c02126c9a extends removeSecrets to SENSITIVE_LONGFORM. git show b7f03866921f8e8d8b936c949ab6c19698b21954 changes MongoDB connectionString from STRING to PASSWORD. git show cc0fd3274b0f36c2510759218eb3616980236f93 changes Firebase privateKey from STRING to SENSITIVE_LONGFORM; because the prior two commits are ancestors, cc0fd3274b0f36c2510759218eb3616980236f93 is the final direct closure commit.

Tag-tree checks show 3.39.19 still has MongoDB connectionString=STRING and Firebase privateKey=STRING, while 3.39.20 has PASSWORD and SENSITIVE_LONGFORM respectively. git tag --contains cc0fd3274b0f36c2510759218eb3616980236f93 begins at 3.39.20, and git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the final fix is contained in advisory-patched tag 3.40.0. This also establishes that the repository's earliest fixed 3.39 tag is narrower than the advisory's conservative <3.40.0 range.

git cat-file commit 28329d7f6b1f7b532665685af78e51827ac80c7e provides the only AI-attribution evidence considered: human author/committer mike12345567, a plain commit message, no trailers, and no AI or bot marker.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins with a raw datasource API design, but the advisory-specific low-privilege route was not functional at dd16c84ecd6feb13b5c3489abf5eea1a218d9456 because the route captured id while the controller dereferenced datasourceId. Commit 28329d7f6b1f7b532665685af78e51827ac80c7e is therefore the smallest real BIC for the TABLE/READ attack path: it changes the parameter to datasourceId, immediately enabling an authenticated table reader with a known datasource ID to retrieve the full stored config. MongoDB's STRING-typed connection URI already existed, and Firebase later added a STRING-typed private key. When b659060beb4246ad943b4660fb06f7a823d12a3d introduced the intended write-only redaction control in 2023, its PASSWORD-only policy left both credentials readable; later support for SENSITIVE_LONGFORM still required the field declarations to be corrected. The minimum closing sequence is 330c1c9c2984bab330456b6be6921f8c02126c9a, b7f03866921f8e8d8b936c949ab6c19698b21954, and final closure cc0fd3274b0f36c2510759218eb3616980236f93. The vulnerable definitions are present in 3.39.19 and corrected in 3.39.20 and 3.40.0. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent human commit, not a move, refactor, backport, release aggregate, or squash, and its commit object has no AI marker; under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
